newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: FOCUS - KLM to slash costs as profits flag.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - KLM to slash costs as profits flag.

text.p: Dutch airline KLM unveiled an ambitious three-year programme to boost earnings on Tuesday after first-half operating profits nose-dived 47 percent.
First half operating profit fell to 262 million guilders ($155 million) from 497 million guilders, eroded by increased fuel costs, a higher wage bill and sub-contractor costs.
However, net profit rose to 529 million guilders from 437 million, swollen by profits on the sale and revaluation of its preferred shareholding in U.S. partner Northwest Airlines .
Announcing the restructuring programme, "Focus 2000", KLM president and chief executive officer Pieter Bouw said drastic measures were necessary to ensure the airline's healthy future.
"We are...obliged to implement a programme which will improve our operating results by at least 1.5 billion guilders in a period of three years," he told a results news conference.
Only then would the airline be able to hold on to its profitability goal of a 14 percent return on equity, he said.
Bouw said two-thirds of the improvement would have to come from cost reductions throughout the organisation with the remainder coming from increased revenues.
"Fundamental change is required, touching every sector of our company," he said, adding: "There will be no sacred cows."
Measures mooted include the transfer of low-profit or unprofitable routes to cheaper European partner airlines such as Air UK or Eurowings and outsourcing various support services.
In addition KLM will review its relationship with intermediaries such as travel agents and forwarders, in the quest for creative solutions to reduce distribution costs.

Asked about the timetable for implementation, Bouw said performance targets had been issued to the various operating units and that a consolidated plan of action would be put forward in January next year.
"But in the meantime those (measures) which can be implemented quickly will of course be implemented quickly," he added.
KLM said net profit for the current 1996-97 year ending next March 31 would be down some 150 million guilders on the previous year's record 547 million, excluding restructuring charges.
Finance director Rob Abrahamsen said KLM could not yet put a firm figure on the likely costs of restructuring.
"It is still too early to say with any clarity that the (restructuring) charges will amount to X or Y or Z," he told journalists.
On the Amsterdam Stock Exchange KLM shares rose 1.80 guilders on the news to 43.70 in late afternoon trade.
Analysts welcomed news of the restructuring programme, saying it was a necessary step to improve the quality of KLM's earnings.
"The restructuring programme is badly needed to compensate tariff pressure from market liberalisation in Europe," said Thibaud de Guerre, airlines analyst with ING Barings.
KLM said it expected airline consolidation within Europe to continue, adding that it was still searching for a strong European partner itself but had nothing firm to announce yet.
